subject: Re: Kestrel - fastpath SLA authorization and operational runbook
messages:
From: Evan Walker <evan.walker@kestrel.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@kestrel.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fastpath SLA request for pilot

Diego —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Kestrel's product team is keen to run the pilot but we need a stronger operational commitment than the standard hosted tier. Specifically, we need a documented path to a P95 sub-80ms response for our real-time inference flow during business hours (US-PST) and a 99.9% monthly availability target for the pilot window.

Can Redwood provide:
- A simple SLA matrix (P95 & availability) you’ll commit to for the pilot window (60 days)
- Runbook describing escalation paths, on-call contacts, and automatic fallback behavior if the fast model variant trips thresholds
- Any operational constraints (regions, throughput caps, supported concurrency) that would affect performance guarantees

I’ve CC'd our legal/contract team so we can start parallel tracks. Evan

--
Evan Walker
Head of Ops, Kestrel AI
ops@kestrel.ai
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Walker <evan.walker@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Contracts <contracts@kestrel.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fastpath SLA request for pilot

Thanks Evan — this is the right scope to move quickly. High level: we can support a pilot with elevated commitments, but it requires coordination across product (model variants + quant profiles), dedicated routing policy, and a short operational runbook. I’m looping Marcus (runtime) and Priya (CS/SLAs) to confirm constraints.

Quick answers up front:
- We can offer an internal Fastpath SLA for pilot: P95 < 80ms (US-PST business hours) and 99.9% monthly availability, conditional on agreed capacity reservation and a conservative throughput cap to avoid queueing-based variance.
- Runbook: we’ll produce a pilot runbook that includes on-call roster, fallback mapping (auto-fail to a slightly larger model variant), and scripted cache-warm steps.
- Constraints: requirement for capacity reservation (minimum GPU share for pilot) and pinned model version. Cross-region traffic will not be covered by the fastpath SLA.

I’ll attach an initial SLA matrix and draft runbook for your review — Marcus, Priya: please review the attached matrix and call out any technical caveats we should add before I send to Kestrel.

Thanks,
Diego

Attachments: kestrel-sla-matrix.xlsx, fastpath-runbook-v2.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fastpath SLA request for pilot

Diego — looked through the matrix. Technical caveats to surface to Kestrel:

1) Guarantees assume a pinned model + quantization profile (we can supply the profile). Any model upgrades mid-pilot require revalidation and may void the fastpath SLA until verified.
2) P95 measurement methodology: we’ll measure on Redwood edge across requests routed to the reserved pool; latency excludes client retry time. We should include a short paragraph with the exact telemetry tags so Kestrel can align.
3) Fallback behavior: automatic failover to a larger model variant is safe but increases token cost and increases latency to ~200-300ms; we recommend an automatic circuit-breaker with alerting rather than immediate customer-facing failover.

I’ve added a short CSV mapping of fallback variants (redwood-fallback-mapping.csv) and annotated the runbook PDF with operational triggers.

—Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Contracts <contracts@kestrel.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Walker <evan.walker@kestrel.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 10:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fastpath SLA request for pilot - legal points

Diego / Priya —

Legal here. A few items we need to confirm before any signature:
- Liquidated damages: Kestrel prefers a credit-based remedy for missed SLA targets rather than termination rights for pilot. Is that acceptable?
- Data handling: during the pilot we need confirmation that telemetry logs will be retained for 90 days and accessible via a shared S3 location for incident investigation.
- Subpoena/compliance: we need an affirmative statement about data residency for requests from EU customers (note: pilot is US-only but we require the clause for our controls).

If Redwood can confirm the credit remedy, 90-day telemetry retention, and a short data residency statement, we can draft a pilot addendum.

Thanks,
Contracts — Kestrel
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Walker <evan.walker@kestrel.ai>, Contracts <contracts@kestrel.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fastpath SLA request for pilot - confirmations and next steps

Evan / Contracts —

We can move forward on the following points for the 60-day pilot:

1) Credit-based remedy: accepted for pilot (credit schedule in attached SLA matrix). Any escalations beyond credits will be treated under our standard enterprise escalation path.
2) Telemetry retention: Redwood will retain telemetry and request/response timing logs for 90 days and provide an S3 snapshot on an agreed cadence. We’ll include the telemetry tags (edge.latency.p95, route, pool_id) in the runbook so you can map incidents.
3) Data residency statement: pilot will be US-only; we will include a short clause that no EU processing will occur during the pilot and that Redwood’s Private deployments support alternative residency on request (enterprise terms).

Operational next steps:
- Priya: please confirm required capacity reservation (min GPU share) so we can send a proposal; we recommend a 2x safety buffer for the pilot initial week.
- Marcus: finalize annotated runbook and push the fallback mapping to the shared workspace.
- Laura: I’ll need your approval on the exec-level note for our SRE rotation covering the pilot (we’ll keep high-touch monitoring during the first 14 days).

We’ll annex the runbook and SLA matrix to a short pilot addendum for signature. Evan — if that aligns, Contracts can expect a redline-ready addendum tomorrow.

Diego
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0198
